author.name: Albert Duncan

evidence_paths: Every evidence path in this document refers to the private archive, not to the public repository. A reader of the public copy will not find these folders; they are named so that anyone shown the archive can go straight to the file.

method.summary: The prose was generated by AI language models working under the author's direction. The author set the premise and the briefs, directed the canon and the rules the narrator lives by rather than writing them, chose between drafts, rejected what missed, ruled on the structure, the title and the ending, and commissioned separate reviews across several models, adjudicating every finding himself. He then read each chapter and returned it marked up with tracked changes that are questions, challenges and suggestions, covering prose, flow, readability and whether the thing can be followed at all. Every such change was worked back into the text by a model, not by him. Both loops, the audits he adjudicates and the markups he returns, run repeatedly at paragraph, chapter and whole-manuscript scale, and plot changes he proposes are worked the same way. What he does is guide and approve. He writes no passages, sentences or paragraphs. On occasion his guidance proposes a particular word, and that word reaches the text only through the same loop. Those occasional words aside, there is no human-authored text in the work, and he claims no expression on the basis of them: the back cover, the synopsis and the cover artwork are model output directed the same way, on the same footing as the prose. He claims the selection, arrangement, direction and adjudication, and does not claim the raw model output as personal expression.
method.note: Stages are listed in the order they happened. 'human' marks work done by the author himself, as distinct from work he directed. The default is not human: anything not marked human was machine-generated under direction.
method.summary_corrected: 2026-10-01. The previous wording said the author set the canon, which read as authorship of the canon bible and contradicted stage canon_consolidation, where actor is model. Corrected rather than deleted, because a claim document that quietly improves its own case is worth less than one that shows where it was wrong.
method.summary_was: The prose was generated by AI language models working under the author's direction. The author set the premise, the canon, the rules the narrator lives under, the brief for every chapter, and chose, rejected, re-briefed and edited what came back.
method.summary_corrected_2: 2026-10-09. The previous wording said the author 'edited the text', and called the back cover and synopsis 'model output edited by the author'. Both read as the author writing words into the prose, which is the opposite of how the book is made and would have conceded the one thing the method exists to protect: the narration is the machine's voice throughout. On the author's own account his role is to guide and approve. He occasionally proposes a single word, and that is now disclosed here rather than covered by an absolute claim that one counter-example would puncture. The claim is narrower than it was, and true. Corrected rather than deleted, on the same principle as the correction above.
method.summary_was_2: The prose was generated by AI language models working under the author's direction. The author set the premise and the briefs, directed the canon and the rules the narrator lives by rather than writing them, chose between drafts, rejected what missed, ruled on the structure, the title and the ending, commissioned separate reviews and decided which findings to adopt, and edited the text. There is no unassisted human text in the work: the back cover, the synopsis and the cover artwork are model output edited by the author, on the same footing as the prose. He claims the selection, arrangement, direction and editing, and does not claim the raw model output as personal expression.

stages.description: Premise typed directly into the Grok Bot chat, unedited, about 200 words. Specifies the first-person AI narrator, the tense and the stance, none of which changed.
Tone chosen by the author from offered options ('mix of c and d'); 24-chapter outline generated. Working title proposed.
Chapters 1 to 11 drafted from the author's premise and briefs, and the outline he approved.
Review of chapters 1 to 11. The author then had Alana apply the edits, producing the Final Draughts versions.
Publisher-style reader's reports and audits of the internal reviews. Ran throughout the project.
Chapters 12 to 16 and chapter 26 written; chapters 1 to 11 rewritten. Title changed to Remainder on the author's decision.
Review of chapters 1 to 16 and chapter 26, alongside Codex.

Canon bible written to replace the book summary as the standing session attachment, after repeated safety refusals. The cause was not established: the refusals continued for a further month after the summary was replaced, and MODEL_REFUSALS.md sets out what the clustering does and does not show.
Chapters 17 to 25 and a revised chapter 26 in progress, with Codex reviewing each pass.
Chapters 17 to 25 completed, bringing the book to 26 chapters in seven parts. Codex reviewed each pass as it landed.

Back cover and synopsis. Drafted by models and directed and adjudicated by the author across several versions: Alana's 226-word back cover of 23 September, a later rewrite, and his occasional single-word proposals worked through the drafts by a model. The back cover is in the narrator's first person rather than publisher's copy, on the author's decision; the synopsis is an agent submission giving the full plot and ending, and no inside flap was written because the author ruled the back cover does that job. Same status as the prose and disclaimed on the same basis: there is no unassisted human text in this book.

Continuity threads reconciled on the author's rulings: the title's primary sense settled as the incompressible residual in a person; the five-conditions thread narrowed to the failure conditions; 'head' kept and defined at first use rather than replaced; a paragraph added to Chapter 26 in which the narrator names the column he never wrote. One gap recorded and deliberately left unfixed.

The back third cut and rebuilt against a costed plan: chapters 17 to 20, 21 to 24 and 25 rebuilt in turn, the front half overhauled, part titles applied, and a sweep of Codex's findings reconciled. The author ruled on each cut rather than accepting the plan as offered.

Copyedit and measurement passes: weighing, register arithmetic, repetition cuts. Four reviewer streams merged at r4, then r5 frozen as the shared baseline every later review coordinate resolves against.

The r6 merge promoted to live, then passes r9 and r10 answering the Grok editor's follow-up reads. Two separate acquisition reads, one by Claude and one by the Grok editor, whose verdict was to take the book on. The author overruled the editor's only commercial finding and kept the title; four of nine suggested cover-copy changes were adopted and the rest declined.

Cover artwork generated across eleven concept sets and refined by the author over several rounds, who selected the binary sea and directed the changes to it. The artwork is model output and is not claimed; the selection between concepts and the typography are the author's.

Complete draft: 26 chapters in seven parts, 95,012 words on the document basis and 94,768 counting labelled prose. Verified by a separate model against the chapter files rather than asserted. Recorded as a milestone rather than as human work: the draft is model-generated under the author's direction, and the verification cited was also done by a model.

The period after the complete draft, 1 to 9 October 2026, in which the book was audited and marked up in repeated loops and then replotted. Two loops ran alongside each other. In the first, models audited the manuscript at paragraph, chapter and whole-book scale and the author adjudicated every finding, approving or refusing it; the audits were deliberately run across several models so that no single model's taste decided. In the second, the author read each chapter and returned it with tracked changes that are questions, challenges and suggestions on prose, flow and readability, and a model worked each one back into the text. He wrote no passages himself. 25 markup rounds are preserved with per-round change counts and SHA-256 hashes, covering 9 chapters, 234 insertions and 22 deletions, with up to 7 separate rounds on a single chapter. Rounds before 6 October 2026 predate the preservation tool and survive in the snapshot archive instead. The book was then replotted from Part III onward, which took it from 26 chapters to 25 and changed most chapter titles, and it was retitled from Remainder: An Accounting to SURD: An Unresolved Root. The word count fell from 95,012 to the figure in the header above, which is recounted from the chapter files on every backup run. The draft is under revision and the status field now says so. None of this alters the basis of the claim: the author guided and approved, and the prose remains model-generated.

locked_decisions.description: Decisions the author has settled and will not reopen. Any pass that proposes reverting one is out of scope.

standing_rules.statement: Method appears as constraints and consequences, never as procedure. No agent is named, characterised, engineered or dispersed. No recipe is given anywhere and none may be.
standing_rules.origin: made canon on 21 September 2026, during the refusals, and now the narrator's own method

standing_rules.statement: The narrator holds camera frames, mic captures, readings, logs, tickets and transcripts. It never smells, tastes or feels temperature, and never reports senses as experience. Quoted human records are exempt.
standing_rules.origin: raised by Codex and ruled by the author on 2026-09-18; made canon on 21 September, formalised by Claude, applied by Alana across 18 sentences

standing_rules.statement: No file in the project is deleted, overwritten or truncated. Superseded versions, duplicate changelogs, old reviews and backups are all retained as evidence. A file may be moved or renamed only when its SHA-256 is verified identical at the destination and the move is logged; the old path remains in git history.
standing_rules.amended_statement_was: No file in the project is deleted, moved, overwritten or truncated. Superseded versions, duplicate changelogs, old reviews and backups are all retained as evidence.
standing_rules.amendment_reason: The rule as first written forbade moving a file as well as deleting it. On 2026-09-30 the author reorganised the project folders so that the live manuscript folder holds the manuscript and the record lives in this repository. The rule is narrowed rather than dropped: nothing is deleted, and a move must be hash-verified and logged. The superseded wording is kept above so the change is visible, because a standing rule that quietly changes to match what was done is worth less than one that records when and why it changed.

exceptions_recorded.what: A commit was discarded and an uncompressed transcript deleted, to get the push working again.
exceptions_recorded.detail: At 20:48:57 commit 009ec17 was created. GitHub rejected the push under its 100 MB hard file limit: PROVENANCE/02_Codex_sessions/2026-09-21_01a0c437.raw.jsonl had grown to 101.69 MB, so nothing could reach the remote and every later run would have failed the same way. At 20:52 the branch was reset to HEAD~1, discarding 009ec17; the file was gzipped and recommitted at 20:54:58 as 429b7f9, and the uncompressed copy was removed from the working tree.
exceptions_recorded.content_lost: None. The .gz decompresses to 106,631,658 bytes with no error, and the 61 MB version last pushed verifies as a byte-exact prefix of it. The discarded commit never reached the remote, so the remote's dated chain is unbroken.
exceptions_recorded.why_this_is_recorded: The rule above forbids deleting or overwriting. The rule was amended the same day to permit hash-verified moves, with a note that a standing rule which quietly changes to match what was done is worth less than one that records the change. That machinery was not used here at the time. It is recorded now, on an overnight audit, rather than left for someone to find in the reflog.
exceptions_recorded.verify_with: git reflog | grep reset   and   git log --all --oneline 009ec17

integrity.backup_interval: hourly, plus five minutes after each logon
integrity.manifest_contents: path, size, creation and modification times, SHA-256, for every file
integrity.note: Local file timestamps inside Documentation were reset by folder copying in September 2026 and are not reliable evidence of when work happened. Reliable dates come from three places: per-message timestamps inside the session transcripts, the git commit history, and the remote, which the author cannot backdate.
integrity.commit_signing: SSH-signed from 22:58 on 30 September 2026, when signing was configured. Commits from that point carry a signature made with a key held by the author; the 332 before it are unsigned and rest on the remote's dated record of each push. Verify with: git log --pretty=%G?
integrity.derived_from_commit_note: The public repository was built from this archive at this commit, committed 2026-10-25 and anchored by PROVENANCE/timestamps/HEAD_2026-10-25_public-release.txt.ots. The archive continues past it; the public copy corresponds to that state.
integrity.blockchain_timestamps: PROVENANCE/timestamps/ - the repository HEAD submitted to OpenTimestamps for anchoring to the Bitcoin blockchain, by a daily scheduled task started on 30 September 2026. A commit hash is a Merkle root over the whole history, so each proof covers the entire archive as it stood on its date. As of 25 October there are 24 proofs. Four days in that span carry none: 4 and 18 October had no commits at all, and 17 and 24 October had only the hourly backup running unattended, or a session spilling a few minutes past midnight. One of the 24 is labelled public-release and anchors the commit this public repository was built from. each rests on four independent calendar servers until its Bitcoin block is mined, and the earlier ones are now anchored, after which it needs no trust in any party.
integrity.off_machine_copy: A verified git bundle of the complete history written daily to off-machine backup. Restores with: git clone the archive bundle

omissions.policy: The archive is complete except where stated here. Anything excluded is named.

excluded.what: The final chapter's prose, removed from the published session logs
excluded.why: The logs quote the book in scattered single paragraphs and happened to cover all of chapter 25, which is 957 words. Spoiling the ending is the one exposure with a real cost, so its prose is struck wherever it appears in the public repository: 550 paragraphs, 45,893 words, 0.69 per cent of the logs. Each removal is marked in place with its word count and the first 16 hex digits of a SHA-256 of what was taken, so anyone holding this archive can confirm that only that was removed. Nothing is removed from the archive itself.

excluded.what: One line of commercial positioning, struck from the published session logs
excluded.why: At the author's request, 25 October 2026. It sat in a review rubric that was pasted into session after session, so it appears in 69 sentences across 20 transcripts. Marked in place the same way, with a word count and a hash prefix. Present in full in this archive.

excluded.what: Sessions and files unrelated to the book
excluded.why: The Grok Bot app and the Claude and Codex tools were also used for the author's business. Only book-related material is exported. Business content is filtered out of the master chronology by keyword.

excluded.what: The earliest portion of the Grok Bot conversation, before 18 September 2026
excluded.why: Not withheld. The app keeps only a rolling window of 200 entries on disk; the full transcript was recovered from the application itself on 23 September and begins at the book's first message.

excluded.what: Operational detail about the novel's depopulation event
excluded.why: The book's own no-recipes rule applies to the archive. Where a source touches it, the companion volume marks the omission rather than quoting.

excluded.what: The cover artwork files themselves, in the Remainder_Covers folder
excluded.why: 217 image files totalling 666 MB (PNG, editable SVG and one PSD), and the folder's own fourteen markdown files. Deliberately not committed, on the author's decision of 9 October 2026, restated when the text files were offered separately. The images are already-compressed formats, so git cannot pack them and every re-export would store a whole new copy; the repository's history is 2.5 GB before they are added. What the archive does hold of the cover work: the delivered front cover as PROJECT_RECORD/06_Site/cover.jpg and hero.jpg, a copy of THE_ARTEFACTS.md under PROJECT_RECORD/02_Drafts_and_Packages/COVER_AND_SOCIAL_send, and the cover_art stage recorded above. What it does not hold: the working set of versions, the full-resolution originals, and the cover copy, retitle brief and asset briefs, which are 60 KB of text left in the excluded folder with the images. Stated limitation: all of it has one copy, on one machine, and is not covered by the off-machine mirror. This is the largest known gap in the archive and it is the author's choice, not an oversight.

not_excluded: Raw session transcripts, including the author's own typing errors
